A system prompt is a block of instructions that developers place at the start of every conversation with a language model. It tells the assistant who it is, how formal to sound, and which topics are out of scope. Users usually never see it, which is why some people treat it as a secret.

Security teams advise against relying on that secrecy. Researchers have repeatedly shown that determined users can coax a model into repeating its instructions, so a system prompt should be written as if it could become public. Credentials, customer data and anything legally sensitive belong in separate systems with proper access control.
